title: コミュニケーション・デザイン実践
subtitle: Practical Communication Design
educationalGoal: Communication can be defined as the process by which human beings convey and mutually understand intentions, emotions, and thoughts through interpersonal relationships. This course focuses specifically on logic, which plays a crucial role in the transmission and understanding of thought. By examining everyday language from the perspective of elementary logic, students will refine their logical skills and acquire the ability to understand others' reasoning accurately and to communicate their own claims clearly and effectively.
advice:
Communication refers to the process by which human beings convey and mutually understand intentions, emotions, and thoughts through interpersonal relationships.This definition indicates that communication encompasses a wide variety of interactive processes of transmission and understanding. Naturally, it is not possible for this course to cover all such aspects.

Accordingly, this course focuses on logic as a key perspective for understanding and conveying thought. From the standpoint of logic, students will learn fundamental concepts and skills necessary for accurately understanding others' reasoning and for expressing their own arguments in a precise manner.

To achieve these aims, the course uses Shigeki Noya's 『まったくゼロからの論理学』 as the main textbook. This book consists of two major parts: Part I, Logic in Everyday Language, and Part II, Constructing a Symbolic Language for Logic. Following the approach recommended in the textbook’s introduction, this course primarily works through Part II while incorporating relevant content from Part I as appropriate. Through reexamining everyday language from the viewpoint of elementary logic, students will aim to refine their logical competence.
books: 野矢茂樹（2020）『まったくゼロからの論理学』、岩波書店

Explain the definitions of negation, conjunction, disjunction, and conditionals, and construct truth tables.
Accurately understand the meanings of universal and existential propositions and express them appropriately.
Accurately understand and express the meaning of written texts based on logical principles and laws.

achievementLevels.ideal:
・Accurately explain what logic is as an academic discipline through explanations of propositions and deduction.
・Accurately explain the definitions of negation, conjunction, disjunction, and conditionals, and construct truth tables for propositions.
・Accurately explain basic logical laws, including the law of non-contradiction, the law of excluded middle, De Morgan’s laws, and contraposition.
・Accurately understand and express the meanings of universal and existential propositions.
・Accurately understand and express the meanings of written texts based on logical principles.
achievementLevels.standard:
・Explain what logic is as an academic discipline in a generally accurate manner through explanations of propositions and deduction.
・Explain the definitions of negation, conjunction, disjunction, and conditionals in a generally accurate manner, and construct truth tables for propositions.
・Explain basic logical laws, including the law of non-contradiction, the law of excluded middle, De Morgan’s laws, and contraposition, in a generally accurate manner.
・Generally understand and express the meanings of universal and existential propositions.
・Generally understand and express the meanings of written texts based on logical principles.

              Communication refers to the process by which human beings convey and mutually understand intentions, emotions, and thoughts through interpersonal relationships.This definition indicates that communication encompasses a wide variety of interactive processes of transmission and understanding. Naturally, it is not possible for this course to cover all such aspects.

Accordingly, this course focuses on logic as a key perspective for understanding and conveying thought. From the standpoint of logic, students will learn fundamental concepts and skills necessary for accurately understanding others' reasoning and for expressing their own arguments in a precise manner.

To achieve these aims, the course uses Shigeki Noya's 『まったくゼロからの論理学』 as the main textbook. This book consists of two major parts: Part I, Logic in Everyday Language, and Part II, Constructing a Symbolic Language for Logic. Following the approach recommended in the textbook’s introduction, this course primarily works through Part II while incorporating relevant content from Part I as appropriate. Through reexamining everyday language from the viewpoint of elementary logic, students will aim to refine their logical competence.
